title: PERFORM UNTIL EXIT (an inline loop left only by EXIT PERFORM)
shapes: PERFORM UNTIL EXIT ... IF WS-I > 12 EXIT PERFORM END-IF ... END-PERFORM, then PERFORM 2000-ROUND (PAYCALC)
asserts: An inline loop: no edge from its header; the PERFORM after it belongs to the paragraph.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If the UNTIL phrase with the EXIT reserved word is specified, execution proceeds exactly as if the same PERFORM statement were coded with condition-1 specified, except that condition-1 never evaluates as true.

notes: New in Enterprise COBOL 6.4 (Summary of changes: PERFORM ... UNTIL EXIT support); it does not compile on 6.3 or earlier. No gitgalaxy issue: an IBM dialect corner planted ahead of any defect.

phantoms.why: an inline PERFORM (line 58) names no procedure; UNTIL is part of its header
